blocks.body:
## Recorded trip spending is $1,819.53

**The supplied evidence and manual additions support 53 included payments totaling $1,819.53.** Fuel is $989.96 (54.4%); food and drinks are $755.77 (41.5%). This includes the preserved user-confirmed $50 fuel correction and the ten newly reviewed images. It is not a verified complete cost of the family trip: lodging and mileage records were not supplied.

## V2 correction adds $50.00 to recorded spending

The August 17 Maverik purchase in Green River, Wyoming is recorded as **$53.37**, replacing $3.37, following your explicit confirmation. The original printed itemization still reconciles to $3.37 ($3.18 plus $0.19 tax); $53.37 is a **user-confirmed override**, not a newly verified printed amount.

You subsequently confirmed that the additional **$50.00 is fuel**. It is now included in fuel spending, with no unallocated balance. Its gallons, grade, and unit price remain unknown, so it is excluded from fuel-price averages. The known $3.37 convenience-drink allocation and printed tax are unchanged. This replaces one receipt total and does not add another payment.

## Ten additional images add eight payments and $317.64

Three pump photos and seven bank screenshots contribute **$99.73 in fuel, $164.60 in restaurants, and $53.31 in groceries**. Two images support existing purchases and add no spending: a matching $40.21 pump photo and an $8.65 Creamery bank transaction. The Creamery match is a merchant-and-amount assumption, not a transaction-ID confirmation; its bank transaction date places it on August 20. The two separate Andy’s bank charges are retained as separate payments.

**DoorDash / Kneaders is assigned to Utah at your explicit instruction.** The bank’s San Francisco platform billing address is not the purchase location. Its city and map point remain unknown. Bank transaction dates—not posting dates—drive the daily chart. Pump-photo capture dates approximate purchase dates; no printed transaction timestamp is claimed. No missing taxes, tips, items, fuel grades, or posted pump prices are invented.

## The spending total has a clear evidence boundary

**The trip window is August 14–30, 2026, inclusive.** There are 51 included image-backed payments and two manual additions. Ten new images add eight payments; two support previously counted payments. Each final payment is counted once. Line items, subtotals, card-payment sections, and supporting evidence are not counted again.

The daily chart includes 48 payments with assigned dates. Three undated image-backed payments and two manual additions remain outside it. July purchases contribute nothing to the trip comparisons below; only their aggregate exclusion count and amount are public. All amounts are US dollars.

## Fuel accounts for 54.4% of supplied spending

**Fuel leads at $989.96; restaurants and prepared meals follow at $473.16.** Read the bars as all-in spending by what was purchased, rather than by the kind of store. Prepared Maverik meals count as restaurants; gas remains fuel; nonfood Walmart items keep their own categories.

Discounts reduce the related category. Receipt taxes are allocated across item categories where necessary, so mixed-receipt category totals are estimates at the category level even though they reconcile exactly to the charged receipt. Fuel tax is generally embedded in the pump price, not an additional amount. The $0.10 checkout-bag charge is grouped into groceries at your request, not shown as its own category.

The $50.00 confirmed correction remains fuel. New bank-only purchases are allocated by merchant and transaction type as all-in charges; their separate tax, tip, and item composition are unknown. A blank tax field does not mean no tax was paid.
The exact category amounts below make small purchases visible even when their bars are too short to compare. Category transaction counts can overlap when one receipt contains more than one category.

## Restaurants cost about 2.2 times the grocery spending

**Food and drinks total $755.77, or 41.5% of included spending.** Restaurant and prepared-meal purchases total $473.16, including the $50 Utah steakhouse payment. Groceries total $217.03; convenience snacks and drinks add $65.58.

The grocery category includes food and drinks bought at grocery stores and Walmart; convenience snacks/drinks describes those purchases at travel stops and similar outlets. This distinction is useful for planning the next trip, but it does not establish when the food was eaten. No separate steakhouse tax, tip, menu items or purchase date were supplied, so the reported $50 is counted as one all-in payment. Grocery spending includes checkout-bag charges. Bank-only restaurant charges are all-in amounts with no inferred tip or item split.

## Utah and Colorado account for 58.2% of spending

**Utah leads with $631.91, followed by Colorado at $426.86.** These figures include provisionally undated receipts wherever the purchase location is known. Utah also includes the reported $50 steakhouse payment; the $25 miscellaneous estimate remains in the unknown-state group.

The receipts document purchases in Wyoming, Missouri, Illinois and Kentucky as well as the states described in the itinerary. Tennessee has no included, dated trip purchase in the supplied batch. Missing Tennessee spending should not be read as evidence that nothing was spent there. DoorDash / Kneaders contributes $83.75 to Utah by user confirmation, without a guessed city or coordinate.

## Maverik and Smith's lead the merchant totals

**Maverik totals $225.16, followed by Smith's at $178.53.** The ranked chart shows the eight largest merchants; the table retains every included merchant, so smaller stops are not lost.

Costco totals **$137.53**, versus **$83.28 at Walmart**. Every included Costco dollar is fuel, so this is not a comparison of grocery prices. The two July purchases are excluded from these comparisons; their individual details are withheld. Merchant aliases verified as the same business are grouped; fuel and food at the same stop remain separate transactions.
Use the fuel column to distinguish a high merchant total driven by gasoline from one driven by food or other purchases. All merchant totals below use the same included scope.

## Measured fuel averaged $4.649 per gallon, weighted by volume

**Fuel spending is $989.96 across 19 payments with a fuel component.** Eighteen purchases with known volume total $939.96 for 202.187 gallons, giving a paid-amount/volume average of **$4.649/gal**. The remaining $50.00 confirmed fuel allocation has no supplied gallons and is excluded from this average.

Only **16 purchases** have posted unit prices: their $840.23 and 179.718 gallons form a different comparison population. The simple average of their posted prices is **$4.692/gal** and their gallon-weighted posted average is **$4.675/gal**. The two new pump photos show $62.80/14.439 gallons and $36.93/8.030 gallons; derived effective prices are $4.349 and $4.599 per gallon, not verified posted prices. Differences between the overall effective average and posted-price averages now reflect different purchase populations, not merely rounding.

**The lowest printed price is $4.099/gal at Tumbleweed Express in Laramie, WY, on Aug 17, 2026.** The highest is $5.199/gal at Seibert Travel Stop in Seibert, CO, on Aug 29, 2026. The spread is $1.100/gal; it is an observed trip range, not proof of a persistent state or station price advantage.

Fifteen original purchases are labeled Premium and one BP Ultimate; the two new pump photos do not show a grade. The $50 correction also has no grade. Do not compare these mixed/unknown-grade observations with regular-grade averages. July purchases are excluded. Without mileage, MPG and fuel cost per mile cannot be calculated.

## Aug 17 is the highest-spending dated day

**The highest fully dated daily total is $311.08, from 8 purchases on Aug 17, 2026.** The chart shows every day of the trip, using printed receipt dates, bank transaction dates, or approximate local pump-photo capture dates. This helps distinguish travel-day purchase clusters from days with fewer supplied receipts; it does not measure time spent in each state.

The bars sum to $1,677.95, not the full $1,819.53 report total. Another **$141.58 has no complete assigned date**: $66.58 of receipt spending plus $75.00 of manual additions. A zero bar means no supplied dated receipt for that day, not verified zero spending. Undated purchases could change the highest-day result.

## Unknown dates and missing expenses remain visible

**$141.58 remains outside the daily chart:** $66.58 from three undated image-backed purchases plus $75.00 in manual additions. Missing dates are not guessed. The bank-supported Creamery date is provisional because its cross-image match uses merchant and amount.

Bank screenshots do not disclose purchased items or a separate tax/tip split. Pump photos do not show posted prices or grades. Restaurant tips, lodging, mileage, and other absent purchases cannot be recovered from this evidence. Earlier user corrections are retained; original and v1/v2 artifacts remain unchanged.

## The companion maps locate purchases, not a reconstructed driving route

**50 of 53 included payments have a point location, representing $1,660.78.** The remaining $158.75 consists of DoorDash and two manual additions. DoorDash and the steakhouse are assigned to Utah, but neither has a known city or point. Location evidence includes address interpolation, verified businesses, approximate cities, and two new pump-photo GPS locations. City and interpolated points are not GPS observations.

Every public map point is rounded to two decimal places and labeled approximate; merchant and city may still identify a store. Purchase dots do not establish the roads driven, route length, or an exact sequence when dates or times are uncertain.

query.description: Public snapshot of reviewed trip-spending analysis, not a live connection. Original receipts, individual item and payment lookup records, personal identifiers, exact purchase times, street addresses, and private audit evidence are withheld. Selected included fuel-purchase dates, public merchant/city names, grades, quantities and prices remain for comparison. The executable query re-selects this already-sanitized public snapshot for report packaging; it is not the private derivation of the measures. The private calculation queries and original evidence are withheld.
filters: Included trip window: August 14–30, 2026, with undated and manual additions retained in aggregate spending.
Daily spending excludes payments without a complete date; July exclusions are shown only as an aggregate scope group.
metric_definitions: Money is USD. Charged purchase totals are counted once; category amounts include allocated tax and tip where supported.

Fuel quantities and posted unit prices retain three-decimal precision. Effective price uses known positive volume and its paid charges; posted-price statistics use only known posted prices. Unknown-volume fuel counts toward spending, not price averages.
query.sql: SELECT snapshot.datasets AS datasets FROM read_json_auto('report-data.json')
